title: Minimal open DAF grant record, v0.1 (draft, unendorsed)
description: DRAFT, UNENDORSED research output (task P-B4013-03-02, 2026-11-20). One record describes one grant from one donor-advised fund to one recipient. No sponsor, intermediary, standards body or regulator has reviewed or adopted it. Field design follows research/mission-2026-11-14/b40n13-03-g1913-03-schema-and-processor-accounts.md section 3.2 with the wave-40A corrections; rationale in research/mission-2026-11-14/b4013-03-02-daf-grant-record-schema.md. Purpose codes use Candid's Philanthropy Classification System (PCS), licensed CC BY 4.0: 'Philanthropy Classification System (PCS) by Candid, https://taxonomy.candid.org/, CC BY 4.0, https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/'. This schema references PCS codes; it does not reproduce or modify the taxonomy.
$comment: Status: draft, unendorsed. Validated with the keyword subset implemented in scripts/mission_validate_grant_record.py.

grant_id.description: Sponsor-issued identifier of one grant, stable from recommendation to payment. Opaque. Recommended form when shared outside the sponsor: '<sponsor org-id>:<local id>', e.g. 'US-EIN-#########:G-123'.

fund_id.description: Sponsor-scoped identifier of the donor-advised fund the grant is drawn from. Opaque: must not contain the donor's name.

sponsor_id.description: Supporting field. Org-id of the sponsoring organization that legally makes the grant (US-EIN- plus 9 digits).

recipient.description: Recipient organization. The IRS EIN (9 digits, no hyphen) is the primary identifier; an alternative scheme (another org-id, or the sponsor's or platform's internal id) is optional, and stands in for the EIN only when the recipient has none.

scheme.description: An org-id.guide list code (e.g. GB-CHC) or a private scheme prefixed 'x-' (e.g. x-endaoment-org-uuid).

amount.description: Amount recommended or awarded for this grant, as a decimal string with exactly two fractional digits (no floats, no minor units), plus an ISO 4217 alphabetic currency code. Converters must not round: a source amount that is not a whole number of cents is rejected, not coerced.

purpose.description: Coded purpose plus free text. Systems should act on codes; text is untrusted input. At least one of codes or text is required.

codes.description: Up to 5 PCS codes, following Candid's rule for grant details ('not required; can have up to 5 codes').

text.description: Free-text purpose as stated by the donor or sponsor. 511 characters, Endaoment's limit for its purpose field.

restriction_text.description: Supporting field. Binding use restriction the recipient must accept, kept apart from the purpose. Untrusted input.

anonymity.description: Donor disclosure level chosen for this grant: full_contact (name and contact details shared), name_only (name shared, contact withheld), anonymous (neither).

status.description: Lifecycle state: Chariot's five values plus returned (payment came back or check voided).

payment_reference.description: The payment rail and the rail's own reference (ACH trace number, check number, provider transaction id, on-chain transaction hash). Required when status is paid or returned.

external_ids.description: Supporting field. Identifiers the grant carries in other systems, e.g. an intermediary's request id that must appear on the remittance advice.

dates.description: UTC timestamps. recommended_at is required; approved_at and updated_at are optional. The payment date sits in payment_reference.paid_date.

timestamp.description: RFC 3339 date-time in UTC with a Z suffix (pattern check only).

pcsCode.description: A PCS code. The facet letter follows the four examples on Candid's developer page: S = subject (SC020000), P = population (PA020000), U = support strategy (UA0000), T = transaction (TA00). Codes may be given at any level shown there (e.g. 'UA0000 or UA'). Code existence is not checked: the full code list could not be read under robots.txt.
